claim: Gross prescribes roller bandages of tolerably stout muslin, free from starch and selvage and well rolled, on an average from two inches and a quarter to two inches and a half in width by eight yards in length.

source.edition: S. D. Gross, A Manual of Military Surgery, second edition, Philadelphia: J. B. Lippincott & Co., 1862 (entered 1861); clean OCR; the archive.org record dates it 1861

quote: The bandages, composed of tolerably stout muslin, should be free from starch and selvage, well rolled, and, on an average, from two inches and a quarter to two inches and a half in width by eight yards in length.

data.item: roller bandage of tolerably stout muslin, free from starch and selvage

scene.may_show: Rolled muslin bandages, plain white, about two and a quarter to two and a half inches wide, ready on the supply table.
